03.4fcaff7c28:
<n>33:2</n> Benedícam Dóminum in omni témpore: * semper laus ejus in ore meo.
<n>33:3</n> In Dómino laudábitur ánima mea: * áudiant mansuéti, et læténtur.
<n>33:4</n> Magnificáte Dóminum mecum: * et exaltémus nomen ejus in idípsum.
<n>33:5</n> Exquisívi Dóminum, et exaudívit me: * et ex ómnibus tribulatiónibus meis erípuit me.
<n>33:6</n> Accédite ad eum, et illuminámini: * et fácies vestræ non confundéntur.
<n>33:7</n> Iste pauper clamávit, et Dóminus exaudívit eum: * et de ómnibus tribulatiónibus ejus salvávit eum.
<n>33:8</n> Immíttet Ángelus Dómini in circúitu timéntium eum: * et erípiet eos.
<n>33:9</n> Gustáte, et vidéte quóniam suávis est Dóminus: * beátus vir, qui sperat in eo.
<n>33:10</n> Timéte Dóminum, omnes sancti ejus: * quóniam non est inópia timéntibus eum.
<n>33:11</n> Dívites eguérunt et esuriérunt: * inquiréntes autem Dóminum non minuéntur omni bono.
<n>33:12</n> Veníte, fílii, audíte me: * timórem Dómini docébo vos.
<n>33:13</n> Quis est homo qui vult vitam: * díligit dies vidére bonos?
<n>33:14</n> Próhibe linguam tuam a malo: * et lábia tua ne loquántur dolum.
<n>33:15</n> Divérte a malo, et fac bonum: * inquíre pacem, et perséquere eam.
<n>33:16</n> Óculi Dómini super justos: * et aures ejus in preces eórum.
<n>33:17</n> Vultus autem Dómini super faciéntes mala: * ut perdat de terra memóriam eórum.
<n>33:18</n> Clamavérunt justi, et Dóminus exaudívit eos: * et ex ómnibus tribulatiónibus eórum liberávit eos.
<n>33:19</n> Juxta est Dóminus iis, qui tribuláto sunt corde: * et húmiles spíritu salvábit.
<n>33:20</n> Multæ tribulatiónes justórum: * et de ómnibus his liberábit eos Dóminus.
<n>33:21</n> Custódit Dóminus ómnia ossa eórum: * unum ex his non conterétur.
<n>33:22</n> Mors peccatórum péssima: * et qui odérunt justum, delínquent.
<n>33:23</n> Rédimet Dóminus ánimas servórum suórum: * et non delínquent omnes qui sperant in eo.
03.fe1868719e:
<n>33:2</n> I will bless the Lord at all times, * his praise shall be always in my mouth.
<n>33:3</n> In the Lord shall my soul be praised: * let the meek hear and rejoice.
<n>33:4</n> O magnify the Lord with me; * and let us extol his name together.
<n>33:5</n> I sought the Lord, and he heard me; * and he delivered me from all my troubles.
<n>33:6</n> Come ye to him and be enlightened: * and your faces shall not be confounded.
<n>33:7</n> This poor man cried, and the Lord heard him: * and saved him out of all his troubles.
<n>33:8</n> The Angel of the Lord shall encamp round about them that fear him: * and shall deliver them.
<n>33:9</n> O taste, and see that the Lord is sweet: * blessed is the man that hopeth in him.
<n>33:10</n> Fear the Lord, all ye his saints: * for there is no want to them that fear him.
<n>33:11</n> The rich have wanted, and have suffered hunger: * but they that seek the Lord shall not be deprived of any good.
<n>33:12</n> Come, children, hearken to me: * I will teach you the fear of the Lord.
<n>33:13</n> Who is the man that desireth life: * who loveth to see good days?
<n>33:14</n> Keep thy tongue from evil, * and thy lips from speaking guile.
<n>33:15</n> Turn away from evil and do good: * seek after peace and pursue it.
<n>33:16</n> The eyes of the Lord are upon the just: * and his ears unto their prayers.
<n>33:17</n> But the countenance of the Lord is against them that do evil things: * to cut off the remembrance of them from the earth.
<n>33:18</n> The just cried, and the Lord heard them: * and delivered them out of all their troubles.
<n>33:19</n> The Lord is nigh unto them that are of a contrite heart: * and he will save the humble of spirit.
<n>33:20</n> Many are the afflictions of the just; * but out of them all will the Lord deliver them.
<n>33:21</n> The Lord keepeth all their bones, * not one of them shall be broken.
<n>33:22</n> The death of the wicked is very evil: * and they that hate the just shall be guilty.
<n>33:23</n> The Lord will redeem the souls of his servants: * and none of them that trust in him shall offend.
03.81e3439b94:
<n>32:1</n> Exsultáte, justi, in Dómino: * rectos decet collaudátio.
<n>32:2</n> Confitémini Dómino in cíthara: * in psaltério decem chordárum psállite illi.
<n>32:3</n> Cantáte ei cánticum novum: * bene psállite ei in vociferatióne.
<n>32:4</n> Quia rectum est verbum Dómini, * et ómnia ópera ejus in fide.
<n>32:5</n> Díligit misericórdiam et judícium: * misericórdia Dómini plena est terra.
<n>32:6</n> Verbo Dómini cæli firmáti sunt: * et spíritu oris ejus omnis virtus eórum.
<n>32:7</n> Cóngregans sicut in utre aquas maris: * ponens in thesáuris abýssos.
<n>32:8</n> Tímeat Dóminum omnis terra: * ab eo autem commoveántur omnes inhabitántes orbem.
<n>32:9</n> Quóniam ipse dixit, et facta sunt: * ipse mandávit, et creáta sunt.
<n>32:10</n> Dóminus díssipat consília géntium: * réprobat autem cogitatiónes populórum, et réprobat consília príncipum.
<n>32:11</n> Consílium autem Dómini in ætérnum manet: * cogitatiónes cordis ejus in generatióne et generatiónem.
<n>32:12</n> Beáta gens, cujus est Dóminus, Deus ejus: * pópulus, quem elégit in hereditátem sibi.
<n>32:13</n> De cælo respéxit Dóminus: * vidit omnes fílios hóminum.
<n>32:14</n> De præparáto habitáculo suo * respéxit super omnes, qui hábitant terram.
<n>32:15</n> Qui finxit sigillátim corda eórum: * qui intéllegit ómnia ópera eórum.
<n>32:16</n> Non salvátur rex per multam virtútem: * et gigas non salvábitur in multitúdine virtútis suæ.
<n>32:17</n> Fallax equus ad salútem: * in abundántia autem virtútis suæ non salvábitur.
<n>32:18</n> Ecce, óculi Dómini super metuéntes eum: * et in eis, qui sperant super misericórdia ejus:
<n>32:19</n> Ut éruat a morte ánimas eórum: * et alat eos in fame.
<n>32:20</n> Ánima nostra sústinet Dóminum: * quóniam adjútor et protéctor noster est.
<n>32:21</n> Quia in eo lætábitur cor nostrum: * et in nómine sancto ejus sperávimus.
<n>32:22</n> Fiat misericórdia tua, Dómine, super nos: * quemádmodum sperávimus in te.
03.a96eceaa42:
<n>32:1</n> Rejoice in the Lord, O ye just: * praise becometh the upright.
<n>32:2</n> Give praise to the Lord on the harp; * sing to him with the psaltery, the instrument of ten strings.
<n>32:3</n> Sing to him a new canticle, * sing well unto him with a loud noise.
<n>32:4</n> For the word of the Lord is right, * and all his works are done with faithfulness.
<n>32:5</n> He loveth mercy and judgment; * the earth is full of the mercy of the Lord.
<n>32:6</n> By the word of the Lord the heavens were established; * and all the power of them by the spirit of his mouth:
<n>32:7</n> Gathering together the waters of the sea, as in a vessel; * laying up the depths in storehouses.
<n>32:8</n> Let all the earth fear the Lord, * and let all the inhabitants of the world be in awe of him.
<n>32:9</n> For he spoke and they were made: * he commanded and they were created.
<n>32:10</n> The Lord bringeth to nought the counsels of nations; * and he rejecteth the devices of people, and casteth away the counsels of princes.
<n>32:11</n> But the counsel of the Lord standeth for ever: * the thoughts of his heart to all generations.
<n>32:12</n> Blessed is the nation whose God is the Lord: * the people whom he hath chosen for his inheritance.
<n>32:13</n> The Lord hath looked from heaven: * he hath beheld all the sons of men.
<n>32:14</n> From his habitation which he hath prepared, * he hath looked upon all that dwell on the earth.
<n>32:15</n> He who hath made the hearts of every one of them: * who understandeth all their works.
<n>32:16</n> The king is not saved by a great army: * nor shall the giant be saved by his own great strength.
<n>32:17</n> Vain is the horse for safety: * neither shall he be saved by the abundance of his strength.
<n>32:18</n> Behold the eyes of the Lord are on them that fear him: * and on them that hope in his mercy.
<n>32:19</n> To deliver their souls from death; * and feed them in famine.
<n>32:20</n> Our soul waiteth for the Lord: * for he is our helper and protector.
<n>32:21</n> For in him our heart shall rejoice: * and in his holy name we have trusted.
<n>32:22</n> Let thy mercy, O Lord, be upon us, * as we have hoped in thee.
03.c7dd198416:
<n>39:2</n> Exspéctans exspectávi Dóminum, * et inténdit mihi.
<n>39:3</n> Et exaudívit preces meas: * et edúxit me de lacu misériæ, et de luto fæcis.
<n>39:3</n> Et státuit super petram pedes meos: * et diréxit gressus meos.
<n>39:4</n> Et immísit in os meum cánticum novum, * carmen Deo nostro.
<n>39:4</n> Vidébunt multi, et timébunt: * et sperábunt in Dómino.
<n>39:5</n> Beátus vir, cujus est nomen Dómini spes ejus: * et non respéxit in vanitátes et insánias falsas.
<n>39:6</n> Multa fecísti tu, Dómine, Deus meus, mirabília tua: * et cogitatiónibus tuis non est qui símilis sit tibi.
<n>39:6</n> Annuntiávi et locútus sum: * multiplicáti sunt super númerum.
<n>39:7</n> Sacrifícium et oblatiónem noluísti: * aures autem perfecísti mihi.
<n>39:7</n> Holocáustum et pro peccáto non postulásti: * tunc dixi: Ecce, vénio.
<n>39:8</n> In cápite libri scriptum est de me ut fácerem voluntátem tuam: * Deus meus, vólui, et legem tuam in médio cordis mei.
<n>39:10</n> Annuntiávi justítiam tuam in ecclésia magna, * ecce, lábia mea non prohibébo: Dómine, tu scisti.
<n>39:11</n> Justítiam tuam non abscóndi in corde meo: * veritátem tuam et salutáre tuum dixi.
<n>39:11</n> Non abscóndi misericórdiam tuam et veritátem tuam * a concílio multo.
<n>39:12</n> Tu autem, Dómine, ne longe fácias miseratiónes tuas a me: * misericórdia tua et véritas tua semper suscepérunt me.
<n>39:13</n> Quóniam circumdedérunt me mala, quorum non est númerus: * comprehendérunt me iniquitátes meæ, et non pótui ut vidérem.
<n>39:13</n> Multiplicátæ sunt super capíllos cápitis mei: * et cor meum derelíquit me.
<n>39:14</n> Compláceat tibi, Dómine, ut éruas me: * Dómine, ad adjuvándum me réspice.
<n>39:15</n> Confundántur et revereántur simul, qui quærunt ánimam meam, * ut áuferant eam.
<n>39:15</n> Convertántur retrórsum, et revereántur, * qui volunt mihi mala.
<n>39:16</n> Ferant conféstim confusiónem suam, * qui dicunt mihi: Euge, euge.
<n>39:17</n> Exsúltent et læténtur super te omnes quæréntes te: * et dicant semper: Magnificétur Dóminus: qui díligunt salutáre tuum.
<n>39:18</n> Ego autem mendícus sum, et pauper: * Dóminus sollícitus est mei.
<n>39:18</n> Adjútor meus, et protéctor meus tu es: * Deus meus, ne tardáveris.
03.8bad4a63d4:
<n>39:2</n> With expectation I have waited for the Lord, * and he was attentive to me.
<n>39:3</n> And he heard my prayers, * and brought me out of the pit of misery and the mire of dregs.
<n>39:3</n> And he set my feet upon a rock, * and directed my steps.
<n>39:4</n> And he put a new canticle into my mouth, * a song to our God.
<n>39:4</n> Many shall see, and shall fear: * and they shall hope in the Lord.
<n>39:5</n> Blessed is the man whose trust is in the name of the Lord; * and who hath not had regard to vanities, and lying follies.
<n>39:6</n> Thou hast multiplied thy wonderful works, O Lord my God: * and in thy thoughts there is no one like to thee.
<n>39:6</n> I have declared and I have spoken * they are multiplied above number.
<n>39:7</n> Sacrifice and oblation thou didst not desire; * but thou hast pierced ears for me.
<n>39:7</n> Burnt offering and sin offering thou didst not require: * then said I, Behold I come.
<n>39:8</n> In the head of the book it is written of me that I should do thy will: * O my God, I have desired it, and thy law in the midst of my heart.
<n>39:10</n> I have declared thy justice in a great church, * lo, I will not restrain my lips: O Lord, thou knowest it.
<n>39:11</n> I have not hid thy justice within my heart: * I have declared thy truth and thy salvation.
<n>39:11</n> I have not concealed thy mercy and thy truth * from a great council.
<n>39:12</n> Withhold not thou, O Lord, thy tender mercies from me: * thy mercy and thy truth have always upheld me.
<n>39:13</n> For evils without number have surrounded me; * my iniquities have overtaken me, and I was not able to see.
<n>39:13</n> They are multiplied above the hairs of my head: * and my heart hath forsaken me.
<n>39:14</n> Be pleased, O Lord to deliver me: * look down, O Lord, to help me.
<n>39:15</n> Let them be confounded and ashamed together, that seek after my soul * to take it away.
<n>39:15</n> Let them be turned backward and be ashamed * that desire evils to me.
<n>39:16</n> Let them immediately bear their confusion, * that say to me: ’T is well, ’t is well.
<n>39:17</n> Let all that seek thee rejoice and be glad in thee: * and let such as love thy salvation say always: The Lord be magnified.
<n>39:18</n> But I am a beggar and poor: * the Lord is careful for me.
<n>39:18</n> Thou art my helper and my protector: * O my God, be not slack.
03.29f033ec02:
<n>38:10</n> Ego dixi: In dimídio diérum meórum * vadam ad portas ínferi.
<n>38:11</n> Quæsívi resíduum annórum meórum. * Dixi: Non vidébo Dóminum Deum in terra vivéntium.
<n>38:12</n> Non aspíciam hóminem ultra, * et habitatórem quiétis.
<n>38:13</n> Generátio mea abláta est, et convolúta est a me, * quasi tabernáculum pastórum.
<n>38:14</n> Præcísa est velut a texénte, vita mea: dum adhuc ordírer, succídit me: * de mane usque ad vésperam fínies me.
<n>38:15</n> Sperábam usque ad mane, * quasi leo sic contrívit ómnia ossa mea:
<n>38:16</n> De mane usque ad vésperam fínies me: * sicut pullus hirúndinis sic clamábo, meditábor ut colúmba:
<n>38:17</n> Attenuáti sunt óculi mei, * suspiciéntes in excélsum.
<n>38:18</n> Dómine, vim pátior, respónde pro me. * Quid dicam, aut quid respondébit mihi, cum ipse fécerit?
<n>38:19</n> Recogitábo tibi omnes annos meos * in amaritúdine ánimæ meæ.
<n>38:20</n> Dómine, si sic vívitur, et in tálibus vita spíritus mei, corrípies me, et vivificábis me. * Ecce, in pace amaritúdo mea amaríssima:
<n>38:21</n> Tu autem eruísti ánimam meam ut non períret: * projecísti post tergum tuum ómnia peccáta mea.
<n>38:22</n> Quia non inférnus confitébitur tibi, neque mors laudábit te: * non exspectábunt qui descéndunt in lacum, veritátem tuam.
<n>38:23</n> Vivens vivens ipse confitébitur tibi, sicut et ego hódie: * pater fíliis notam fáciet veritátem tuam.
<n>38:24</n> Dómine, salvum me fac * et psalmos nostros cantábimus cunctis diébus vitæ nostræ in domo Dómini.
03.3d968338a2:
<n>38:10</n> I said: In the midst of my days * I shall go to the gates of hell:
<n>38:11</n> I sought for the residue of my years. * I said: I shall not see the Lord God in the land of the living.
<n>38:12</n> I shall behold man no more, * nor the inhabitant of rest.
<n>38:13</n> My generation is at an end, and it is rolled away from me, * as a shepherd’s tent.
<n>38:14</n> My life is cut off, as by a weaver: whilst I was yet but beginning, he cut me off: * from morning even to night thou wilt make an end of me.
<n>38:15</n> I hoped till morning, * as a lion so hath he broken all my bones:
<n>38:16</n> From morning even to night thou wilt make an end of me. * I will cry like a young swallow, I will meditate like a dove:
<n>38:17</n> My eyes are weakened * looking upward:
<n>38:18</n> Lord, I suffer violence, answer thou for me. * What shall I say, or what shall he answer for me, whereas he himself hath done it?
<n>38:19</n> I will recount to thee all my years * in the bitterness of my soul.
<n>38:20</n> O Lord, if man’s life be such, and the life of my spirit be in such things as these, thou shalt correct me, and make me to live. * Behold in peace is my bitterness most bitter:
<n>38:21</n> But thou hast delivered my soul that it should not perish, * thou hast cast all my sins behind thy back.
<n>38:22</n> For hell shall not confess to thee, neither shall death praise thee: * nor shall they that go down into the pit, look for thy truth.
<n>38:23</n> The living, the living, he shall give praise to thee, as I do this day: * the father shall make thy truth known to the children.
<n>38:24</n> O Lord, save me, and we will sing our psalms all the days of our life * in the house of the Lord.
03.a3f107f457:
<n>34:1</n> Júdica, Dómine, nocéntes me, * expúgna impugnántes me.
<n>34:2</n> Apprehénde arma et scutum: * et exsúrge in adjutórium mihi.
<n>34:3</n> Effúnde frámeam, et conclúde advérsus eos, qui persequúntur me: * dic ánimæ meæ: Salus tua ego sum.
<n>34:4</n> Confundántur et revereántur, * quæréntes ánimam meam.
<n>34:4</n> Avertántur retrórsum, et confundántur * cogitántes mihi mala.
<n>34:5</n> Fiant tamquam pulvis ante fáciem venti: * et Ángelus Dómini coárctans eos.
<n>34:6</n> Fiat via illórum ténebræ et lúbricum: * et Ángelus Dómini pérsequens eos.
<n>34:7</n> Quóniam gratis abscondérunt mihi intéritum láquei sui: * supervácue exprobravérunt ánimam meam.
<n>34:8</n> Véniat illi láqueus, quem ignórat: et cáptio, quam abscóndit, apprehéndat eum: * et in láqueum cadat in ipsum.
<n>34:9</n> Ánima autem mea exsultábit in Dómino: * et delectábitur super salutári suo.
<n>34:10</n> Ómnia ossa mea dicent: * Dómine, quis símilis tibi?
<n>34:10</n> Erípiens ínopem de manu fortiórum ejus: * egénum et páuperem a diripiéntibus eum.
03.ba76da7dfb:
<n>34:1</n> Judge thou, O Lord, them that wrong me: * overthrow them that fight against me.
<n>34:2</n> Take hold of arms and shield: * and rise up to help me.
<n>34:3</n> Bring out the sword, and shut up the way against them that persecute me: * say to my soul: I am thy salvation.
<n>34:4</n> Let them be confounded and ashamed * that seek after my soul.
<n>34:4</n> Let them be turned back and be confounded * that devise against me.
<n>34:5</n> Let them become as dust before the wind: * and let the Angel of the Lord straiten them.
<n>34:6</n> Let their way become dark and slippery; * and let the Angel of the Lord pursue them.
<n>34:7</n> For without cause they have hidden their net for me unto destruction: * without cause they have upbraided my soul.
<n>34:8</n> Let the snare which he knoweth not come upon him: and let the net which he hath hidden catch him: * and into that very snare let them fall.
<n>34:9</n> But my soul shall rejoice in the Lord; * and shall be delighted in his salvation.
<n>34:10</n> All my bones shall say: * Lord, who is like to thee?
<n>34:10</n> Who deliverest the poor from the hand of them that are stronger than he; * the needy and the poor from them that strip him.
03.21b06601cb:
<n>34:11</n> Surgéntes testes iníqui, * quæ ignorábam interrogábant me.
<n>34:12</n> Retribuébant mihi mala pro bonis: * sterilitátem ánimæ meæ.
<n>34:13</n> Ego autem cum mihi molésti essent, * induébar cilício.
<n>34:13</n> Humiliábam in jejúnio ánimam meam: * et orátio mea in sinu meo convertétur.
<n>34:14</n> Quasi próximum, et quasi fratrem nostrum, sic complacébam: * quasi lugens et contristátus, sic humiliábar.
<n>34:15</n> Et advérsum me lætáti sunt, et convenérunt: * congregáta sunt super me flagélla, et ignorávi.
<n>34:16</n> Dissipáti sunt, nec compúncti, tentavérunt me, subsannavérunt me subsannatióne: * frenduérunt super me déntibus suis.
<n>34:17</n> Dómine, quando respícies? * restítue ánimam meam a malignitáte eórum, a leónibus únicam meam.
03.f5f0330536:
<n>34:11</n> Unjust witnesses rising up * have asked me things I knew not.
<n>34:12</n> They repaid me evil for good: * to the depriving me of my soul.
<n>34:13</n> But as for me, when they were troublesome to me, * I was clothed with haircloth.
<n>34:13</n> I humbled my soul with fasting; * and my prayer shall be turned into my bosom.
<n>34:14</n> As a neighbour and as an own brother, so did I please: * as one mourning and sorrowful so was I humbled.
<n>34:15</n> But they rejoiced against me, and came together: * scourges were gathered together upon me, and I knew not.
<n>34:16</n> They were separated, and repented not: they tempted me, they scoffed at me with scorn: * they gnashed upon me with their teeth.
<n>34:17</n> Lord, when wilt thou look upon me? * rescue thou my soul from their malice: my only one from the lions.
03.e393cc1b7e:
<n>34:18</n> Confitébor tibi in ecclésia magna, * in pópulo gravi laudábo te.
<n>34:19</n> Non supergáudeant mihi qui adversántur mihi iníque: * qui odérunt me gratis et ánnuunt óculis.
<n>34:20</n> Quóniam mihi quidem pacífice loquebántur: * et in iracúndia terræ loquéntes, dolos cogitábant.
<n>34:21</n> Et dilatavérunt super me os suum: * dixérunt: Euge, euge, vidérunt óculi nostri.
<n>34:22</n> Vidísti, Dómine, ne síleas: * Dómine, ne discédas a me.
<n>34:23</n> Exsúrge et inténde judício meo: * Deus meus, et Dóminus meus in causam meam.
<n>34:24</n> Júdica me secúndum justítiam tuam, Dómine, Deus meus, * et non supergáudeant mihi.
<n>34:25</n> Non dicant in córdibus suis: Euge, euge, ánimæ nostræ: * nec dicant: Devorávimus eum.
<n>34:26</n> Erubéscant et revereántur simul, * qui gratulántur malis meis.
<n>34:26</n> Induántur confusióne et reveréntia * qui magna loquúntur super me.
<n>34:27</n> Exsúltent et læténtur qui volunt justítiam meam: * et dicant semper: Magnificétur Dóminus qui volunt pacem servi ejus.
<n>34:28</n> Et lingua mea meditábitur justítiam tuam, * tota die laudem tuam.
03.f84270be63:
<n>34:18</n> I will give thanks to thee in a great church; * I will praise thee in a strong people.
<n>34:19</n> Let not them that are my enemies wrongfully rejoice over me: * who have hated me without cause, and wink with the eyes.
<n>34:20</n> For they spoke indeed peaceably to me; * and speaking in the anger of the earth they devised guile.
<n>34:21</n> And they opened their mouth wide against me; * they said: Well done, well done, our eyes have seen it.
<n>34:22</n> Thou hast seen, O Lord, be not thou silent: * O Lord, depart not from me.
<n>34:23</n> Arise, and be attentive to my judgment: * to my cause, my God, and my Lord.
<n>34:24</n> Judge me, O Lord my God according to thy justice, * and let them not rejoice over me.
<n>34:25</n> Let them not say in their hearts: It is well, it is well, to our mind: * neither let them say: We have swallowed him up.
<n>34:26</n> Let them blush: and be ashamed together, * who rejoice at my evils.
<n>34:26</n> Let them be clothed with confusion and shame, * who speak great things against me.
<n>34:27</n> Let them rejoice and be glad, who are well pleased with my justice, * and let them say always: The Lord be magnified, who delights in the peace of his servant.
<n>34:28</n> And my tongue shall meditate thy justice, * thy praise all the day long.
03.a7acff53d9:
<n>36:1</n> Noli æmulári in malignántibus: * neque zeláveris faciéntes iniquitátem.
<n>36:2</n> Quóniam tamquam fænum velóciter aréscent: * et quemádmodum ólera herbárum cito décident.
<n>36:3</n> Spera in Dómino, et fac bonitátem: * et inhábita terram, et pascéris in divítiis ejus.
<n>36:4</n> Delectáre in Dómino: * et dabit tibi petitiónes cordis tui.
<n>36:5</n> Revéla Dómino viam tuam, et spera in eo: * et ipse fáciet.
<n>36:6</n> Et edúcet quasi lumen justítiam tuam: et judícium tuum tamquam merídiem: * súbditus esto Dómino, et ora eum.
<n>36:7</n> Noli æmulári in eo, qui prosperátur in via sua: * in hómine faciénte injustítias.
<n>36:8</n> Désine ab ira, et derelínque furórem: * noli æmulári ut malignéris.
<n>36:9</n> Quóniam qui malignántur, exterminabúntur: * sustinéntes autem Dóminum, ipsi hereditábunt terram.
<n>36:10</n> Et adhuc pusíllum, et non erit peccátor: * et quæres locum ejus et non invénies.
<n>36:11</n> Mansuéti autem hereditábunt terram: * et delectabúntur in multitúdine pacis.
<n>36:12</n> Observábit peccátor justum: * et stridébit super eum déntibus suis.
<n>36:13</n> Dóminus autem irridébit eum: * quóniam próspicit quod véniet dies ejus.
<n>36:14</n> Gládium evaginavérunt peccatóres: * intendérunt arcum suum,
<n>36:14</n> Ut deíciant páuperem et ínopem: * ut trucídent rectos corde.
<n>36:15</n> Gládius eórum intret in corda ipsórum: * et arcus eórum confringátur.
03.5daa8ccfc9:
<n>36:1</n> Be not emulous of evildoers; * nor envy them that work iniquity.
<n>36:2</n> For they shall shortly wither away as grass, * and as the green herbs shall quickly fall.
<n>36:3</n> Trust in the Lord, and do good, * and dwell in the land, and thou shalt be fed with its riches.
<n>36:4</n> Delight in the Lord, * and he will give thee the requests of thy heart.
<n>36:5</n> Commit thy way to the Lord, and trust in him, * and he will do it.
<n>36:6</n> And he will bring forth thy justice as the light, and thy judgment as the noonday: * be subject to the Lord and pray to him.
<n>36:7</n> Envy not the man who prospereth in his way; * the man who doth unjust things.
<n>36:8</n> Cease from anger, and leave rage; * have no emulation to do evil.
<n>36:9</n> For the evildoers shall be cut off: * but they that wait upon the Lord shall inherit the land.
<n>36:10</n> For yet a little while, and the wicked shall not be: * and thou shalt seek his place, and shalt not find it.
<n>36:11</n> But the meek shall inherit the land, * and shall delight in abundance of peace.
<n>36:12</n> The sinner shall watch the just man: * and shall gnash upon him with his teeth.
<n>36:13</n> But the Lord shall laugh at him: * for he foreseeth that his day shall come.
<n>36:14</n> The wicked have drawn out the sword: * they have bent their bow.
<n>36:14</n> To cast down the poor and needy, * to kill the upright of heart.
<n>36:15</n> Let their sword enter into their own hearts, * and let their bow be broken.
03.4dc45e7f79:
<n>36:16</n> Mélius est módicum justo, * super divítias peccatórum multas.
<n>36:17</n> Quóniam brácchia peccatórum conteréntur: * confírmat autem justos Dóminus.
<n>36:18</n> Novit Dóminus dies immaculatórum: * et heréditas eórum in ætérnum erit.
<n>36:19</n> Non confundéntur in témpore malo, et in diébus famis saturabúntur: * quia peccatóres períbunt.
<n>36:20</n> Inimíci vero Dómini mox ut honorificáti fúerint et exaltáti: * deficiéntes, quemádmodum fumus defícient.
<n>36:21</n> Mutuábitur peccátor, et non solvet: * justus autem miserétur et tríbuet.
<n>36:22</n> Quia benedicéntes ei hereditábunt terram: * maledicéntes autem ei disperíbunt.
<n>36:23</n> Apud Dóminum gressus hóminis dirigéntur: * et viam ejus volet.
<n>36:24</n> Cum cecíderit non collidétur: * quia Dóminus suppónit manum suam.
<n>36:25</n> Júnior fui, étenim sénui: * et non vidi justum derelíctum, nec semen ejus quærens panem.
<n>36:26</n> Tota die miserétur et cómmodat: * et semen illíus in benedictióne erit.
<n>36:27</n> Declína a malo, et fac bonum: * et inhábita in sǽculum sǽculi.
<n>36:28</n> Quia Dóminus amat judícium, et non derelínquet sanctos suos: * in ætérnum conservabúntur.
<n>36:28</n> Injústi puniéntur: * et semen impiórum períbit.
<n>36:29</n> Justi autem hereditábunt terram: * et inhabitábunt in sǽculum sǽculi super eam.
03.cc57b57ff2:
<n>36:16</n> Better is a little to the just, * than the great riches of the wicked.
<n>36:17</n> For the arms of the wicked shall be broken in pieces; * but the Lord strengtheneth the just.
<n>36:18</n> The Lord knoweth the days of the undefiled; * and their inheritance shall be for ever.
<n>36:19</n> They shall not be confounded in the evil time; and in the days of famine they shall be filled, * because the wicked shall perish.
<n>36:20</n> And the enemies of the Lord, presently after they shall be honoured and exalted, * shall come to nothing and vanish like smoke.
<n>36:21</n> The sinner shall borrow, and not pay again; * but the just sheweth mercy and shall give.
<n>36:22</n> For such as bless him shall inherit the land: * but such as curse him shall perish.
<n>36:23</n> With the Lord shall the steps of a man be directed, * and he shall like well his way.
<n>36:24</n> When he shall fall he shall not be bruised, * for the Lord putteth his hand under him.
<n>36:25</n> I have been young, and now am old; * and I have not seen the just forsaken, nor his seed seeking bread.
<n>36:26</n> He sheweth mercy, and lendeth all the day long; * and his seed shall be in blessing.
<n>36:27</n> Decline from evil and do good, * and dwell for ever and ever.
<n>36:28</n> For the Lord loveth judgment, and will not forsake his saints: * they shall be preserved for ever.
<n>36:28</n> The unjust shall be punished, * and the seed of the wicked shall perish.
<n>36:29</n> But the just shall inherit the land, * and shall dwell therein for evermore.
03.93da2997dd:
<n>36:30</n> Os justi meditábitur sapiéntiam, * et lingua ejus loquétur judícium.
<n>36:31</n> Lex Dei ejus in corde ipsíus, * et non supplantabúntur gressus ejus.
<n>36:32</n> Consíderat peccátor justum: * et quærit mortificáre eum.
<n>36:33</n> Dóminus autem non derelínquet eum in mánibus ejus: * nec damnábit eum, cum judicábitur illi.
<n>36:34</n> Exspécta Dóminum, et custódi viam ejus: et exaltábit te ut hereditáte cápias terram: * cum períerint peccatóres vidébis.
<n>36:35</n> Vidi ímpium superexaltátum, * et elevátum sicut cedros Líbani.
<n>36:36</n> Et transívi, et ecce non erat: * et quæsívi eum, et non est invéntus locus ejus.
<n>36:37</n> Custódi innocéntiam, et vide æquitátem: * quóniam sunt relíquiæ hómini pacífico.
<n>36:38</n> Injústi autem disperíbunt simul: * relíquiæ impiórum interíbunt.
<n>36:39</n> Salus autem justórum a Dómino: * et protéctor eórum in témpore tribulatiónis.
<n>36:40</n> Et adjuvábit eos Dóminus et liberábit eos: * et éruet eos a peccatóribus, et salvábit eos: quia speravérunt in eo.
03.8b1590c63a:
<n>36:30</n> The mouth of the just shall meditate wisdom: * and his tongue shall speak judgment.
<n>36:31</n> The law of his God is in his heart, * and his steps shall not be supplanted.
<n>36:32</n> The wicked watcheth the just man, * and seeketh to put him to death.
<n>36:33</n> But the Lord will not leave him in his hands; * nor condemn him when he shall be judged.
<n>36:34</n> Expect the Lord and keep his way: and he will exalt thee to inherit the land: * when the sinners shall perish thou shalt see.
<n>36:35</n> I have seen the wicked highly exalted, * and lifted up like the cedars of Libanus.
<n>36:36</n> And I passed by, and lo, he was not: * and I sought him and his place was not found.
<n>36:37</n> Keep innocence, and behold justice: * for there are remnants for the peaceable man.
<n>36:38</n> But the unjust shall be destroyed together: * the remnants of the wicked shall perish.
<n>36:39</n> But the salvation of the just is from the Lord, * and he is their protector in the time of trouble.
<n>36:40</n> And the Lord will help them and deliver them: * and he will rescue them from the wicked, and save them, because they have hoped in him.
03.964ddf212d:
<n>37:2</n> Dómine, ne in furóre tuo árguas me, * neque in ira tua corrípias me.
<n>37:3</n> Quóniam sagíttæ tuæ infíxæ sunt mihi: * et confirmásti super me manum tuam.
<n>37:4</n> Non est sánitas in carne mea a fácie iræ tuæ: * non est pax óssibus meis a fácie peccatórum meórum.
<n>37:5</n> Quóniam iniquitátes meæ supergréssæ sunt caput meum: * et sicut onus grave gravátæ sunt super me.
<n>37:6</n> Putruérunt et corrúptæ sunt cicatríces meæ, * a fácie insipiéntiæ meæ.
<n>37:7</n> Miser factus sum, et curvátus sum usque in finem: * tota die contristátus ingrediébar.
<n>37:8</n> Quóniam lumbi mei impléti sunt illusiónibus: * et non est sánitas in carne mea.
<n>37:9</n> Afflíctus sum, et humiliátus sum nimis: * rugiébam a gémitu cordis mei.
<n>37:10</n> Dómine, ante te omne desidérium meum: * et gémitus meus a te non est abscónditus.
<n>37:11</n> Cor meum conturbátum est, derelíquit me virtus mea: * et lumen oculórum meórum, et ipsum non est mecum.
03.db4633a7af:
<n>37:2</n> Rebuke me not, O Lord, in thy indignation; * nor chastise me in thy wrath.
<n>37:3</n> For thy arrows are fastened in me: * and thy hand hath been strong upon me.
<n>37:4</n> There is no health in my flesh, because of thy wrath: * there is no peace for my bones, because of my sins.
<n>37:5</n> For my iniquities are gone over my head: * and as a heavy burden are become heavy upon me.
<n>37:6</n> My sores are putrified and corrupted, * because of my foolishness.
<n>37:7</n> I am become miserable, and am bowed down even to the end: * I walked sorrowful all the day long.
<n>37:8</n> For my loins are filled with illusions; * and there is no health in my flesh.
<n>37:9</n> I am afflicted and humbled exceedingly: * I roared with the groaning of my heart.
<n>37:10</n> Lord, all my desire is before thee, * and my groaning is not hidden from thee.
<n>37:11</n> My heart is troubled, my strength hath left me, * and the light of my eyes itself is not with me.
03.e3614976c7:
<n>37:12</n> Amíci mei, et próximi mei * advérsum me appropinquavérunt, et stetérunt.
<n>37:12</n> Et qui juxta me erant, de longe stetérunt: * et vim faciébant qui quærébant ánimam meam.
<n>37:13</n> Et qui inquirébant mala mihi, locúti sunt vanitátes: * et dolos tota die meditabántur.
<n>37:14</n> Ego autem tamquam surdus non audiébam: * et sicut mutus non apériens os suum.
<n>37:15</n> Et factus sum sicut homo non áudiens: * et non habens in ore suo redargutiónes.
<n>37:16</n> Quóniam in te, Dómine, sperávi: * tu exáudies me, Dómine, Deus meus.
<n>37:17</n> Quia dixi: Nequándo supergáudeant mihi inimíci mei: * et dum commovéntur pedes mei, super me magna locúti sunt.
<n>37:18</n> Quóniam ego in flagélla parátus sum: * et dolor meus in conspéctu meo semper.
<n>37:19</n> Quóniam iniquitátem meam annuntiábo: * et cogitábo pro peccáto meo.
<n>37:20</n> Inimíci autem mei vivunt, et confirmáti sunt super me: * et multiplicáti sunt qui odérunt me iníque.
<n>37:21</n> Qui retríbuunt mala pro bonis, detrahébant mihi: * quóniam sequébar bonitátem.
<n>37:22</n> Ne derelínquas me, Dómine, Deus meus: * ne discésseris a me.
<n>37:23</n> Inténde in adjutórium meum, * Dómine, Deus, salútis meæ.
03.f1c281e18b:
<n>37:12</n> My friends and my neighbours * have drawn near, and stood against me.
<n>37:12</n> And they that were near me stood afar off: * and they that sought my soul used violence.
<n>37:13</n> And they that sought evils to me spoke vain things, * and studied deceits all the day long.
<n>37:14</n> But I, as a deaf man, heard not: * and as a dumb man not opening his mouth.
<n>37:15</n> And I became as a man that heareth not: * and that hath no reproofs in his mouth.
<n>37:16</n> For in thee, O Lord, have I hoped: * thou wilt hear me, O Lord my God.
<n>37:17</n> For I said: Lest at any time my enemies rejoice over me: * and whilst my feet are moved, they speak great things against me.
<n>37:18</n> For I am ready for scourges: * and my sorrow is continually before me.
<n>37:19</n> For I will declare my iniquity: * and I will think for my sin.
<n>37:20</n> But my enemies live, and are stronger than I: * and they that hate me wrongfully are multiplied.
<n>37:21</n> They that render evil for good, have detracted me, * because I followed goodness.
<n>37:22</n> Forsake me not, O Lord my God: * do not thou depart from me.
<n>37:23</n> Attend unto my help, * O Lord, the God of my salvation.
03.8df1cc86e3:
<n>38:2</n> Dixi: Custódiam vias meas: * ut non delínquam in lingua mea.
<n>38:2</n> Pósui ori meo custódiam, * cum consísteret peccátor advérsum me.
<n>38:3</n> Obmútui, et humiliátus sum, et sílui a bonis: * et dolor meus renovátus est.
<n>38:4</n> Concáluit cor meum intra me: * et in meditatióne mea exardéscet ignis.
<n>38:5</n> Locútus sum in lingua mea: * Notum fac mihi, Dómine, finem meum.
<n>38:5</n> Et númerum diérum meórum quis est: * ut sciam quid desit mihi.
<n>38:6</n> Ecce mensurábiles posuísti dies meos: * et substántia mea tamquam níhilum ante te.
<n>38:6</n> Verúmtamen univérsa vánitas, * omnis homo vivens.
<n>38:7</n> Verúmtamen in imágine pertránsit homo: * sed et frustra conturbátur.
<n>38:7</n> Thesaurízat: * et ignórat cui congregábit ea.
<n>38:8</n> Et nunc quæ est exspectátio mea? Nonne Dóminus? * Et substántia mea apud te est.
<n>38:9</n> Ab ómnibus iniquitátibus meis érue me: * oppróbrium insipiénti dedísti me.
<n>38:10</n> Obmútui, et non apérui os meum, quóniam tu fecísti: * ámove a me plagas tuas.
<n>38:12</n> A fortitúdine manus tuæ ego deféci in increpatiónibus: * propter iniquitátem corripuísti hóminem.
<n>38:12</n> Et tabéscere fecísti sicut aráneam ánimam ejus: * verúmtamen vane conturbátur omnis homo.
<n>38:13</n> Exáudi oratiónem meam, Dómine, et deprecatiónem meam: * áuribus pércipe lácrimas meas.
<n>38:13</n> Ne síleas: quóniam ádvena ego sum apud te, et peregrínus, * sicut omnes patres mei.
<n>38:14</n> Remítte mihi, ut refrígerer priúsquam ábeam, * et ámplius non ero.
03.b31dcd2a31:
<n>38:2</n> I said: I will take heed to my ways: * that I sin not with my tongue.
<n>38:2</n> I have set guard to my mouth, * when the sinner stood against me.
<n>38:3</n> I was dumb, and was humbled, and kept silence from good things: * and my sorrow was renewed.
<n>38:4</n> My heart grew hot within me: * and in my meditation a fire shall flame out.
<n>38:5</n> I spoke with my tongue: * O Lord, make me know my end.
<n>38:5</n> And what is the number of my days: * that I may know what is wanting to me.
<n>38:6</n> Behold thou hast made my days measurable: * and my substance is as nothing before thee.
<n>38:6</n> And indeed all things are vanity: * every man living.
<n>38:7</n> Surely man passeth as an image: * yea, and he is disquieted in vain.
<n>38:7</n> He storeth up: * and he knoweth not for whom he shall gather these things.
<n>38:8</n> And now what is my hope? Is it not the Lord? * And my substance is with thee.
<n>38:9</n> Deliver thou me from all my iniquities: * thou hast made me a reproach to the fool.
<n>38:10</n> I was dumb, and I opened not my mouth, because thou hast done it: * remove thy scourges from me.
<n>38:12</n> The strength of thy hand hath made me faint in rebukes: * thou hast corrected man for iniquity.
<n>38:12</n> And thou hast made his soul to waste away like a spider: * surely in vain is any man disquieted.
<n>38:13</n> Hear my prayer, O Lord, and my supplication: * give ear to my tears.
<n>38:13</n> Be not silent: for I am a stranger with thee, * and a sojourner as all my fathers were.
<n>38:14</n> O forgive me, that I may be refreshed, before I go hence, * and be no more.
03.acf6a01f9b:
<n>39:2</n> Exspéctans exspectávi Dóminum, * et inténdit mihi.
<n>39:3</n> Et exaudívit preces meas: * et edúxit me de lacu misériæ, et de luto fæcis.
<n>39:3</n> Et státuit super petram pedes meos: * et diréxit gressus meos.
<n>39:4</n> Et immísit in os meum cánticum novum, * carmen Deo nostro.
<n>39:4</n> Vidébunt multi, et timébunt: * et sperábunt in Dómino.
<n>39:5</n> Beátus vir, cujus est nomen Dómini spes ejus: * et non respéxit in vanitátes et insánias falsas.
<n>39:6</n> Multa fecísti tu, Dómine, Deus meus, mirabília tua: * et cogitatiónibus tuis non est qui símilis sit tibi.
<n>39:6</n> Annuntiávi et locútus sum: * multiplicáti sunt super númerum.
<n>39:7</n> Sacrifícium et oblatiónem noluísti: * aures autem perfecísti mihi.
<n>39:7</n> Holocáustum et pro peccáto non postulásti: * tunc dixi: Ecce, vénio.
<n>39:8</n> In cápite libri scriptum est de me ut fácerem voluntátem tuam: * Deus meus, vólui, et legem tuam in médio cordis mei.
03.191bad65be:
<n>39:2</n> With expectation I have waited for the Lord, * and he was attentive to me.
<n>39:3</n> And he heard my prayers, * and brought me out of the pit of misery and the mire of dregs.
<n>39:3</n> And he set my feet upon a rock, * and directed my steps.
<n>39:4</n> And he put a new canticle into my mouth, * a song to our God.
<n>39:4</n> Many shall see, and shall fear: * and they shall hope in the Lord.
<n>39:5</n> Blessed is the man whose trust is in the name of the Lord; * and who hath not had regard to vanities, and lying follies.
<n>39:6</n> Thou hast multiplied thy wonderful works, O Lord my God: * and in thy thoughts there is no one like to thee.
<n>39:6</n> I have declared and I have spoken * they are multiplied above number.
<n>39:7</n> Sacrifice and oblation thou didst not desire; * but thou hast pierced ears for me.
<n>39:7</n> Burnt offering and sin offering thou didst not require: * then said I, Behold I come.
<n>39:8</n> In the head of the book it is written of me that I should do thy will: * O my God, I have desired it, and thy law in the midst of my heart.
03.c9e9945d79:
<n>39:10</n> Annuntiávi justítiam tuam in ecclésia magna, * ecce, lábia mea non prohibébo: Dómine, tu scisti.
<n>39:11</n> Justítiam tuam non abscóndi in corde meo: * veritátem tuam et salutáre tuum dixi.
<n>39:11</n> Non abscóndi misericórdiam tuam et veritátem tuam * a concílio multo.
<n>39:12</n> Tu autem, Dómine, ne longe fácias miseratiónes tuas a me: * misericórdia tua et véritas tua semper suscepérunt me.
<n>39:13</n> Quóniam circumdedérunt me mala, quorum non est númerus: * comprehendérunt me iniquitátes meæ, et non pótui ut vidérem.
<n>39:13</n> Multiplicátæ sunt super capíllos cápitis mei: * et cor meum derelíquit me.
<n>39:14</n> Compláceat tibi, Dómine, ut éruas me: * Dómine, ad adjuvándum me réspice.
03.98e7b3ebd5:
<n>39:10</n> I have declared thy justice in a great church, * lo, I will not restrain my lips: O Lord, thou knowest it.
<n>39:11</n> I have not hid thy justice within my heart: * I have declared thy truth and thy salvation.
<n>39:11</n> I have not concealed thy mercy and thy truth * from a great council.
<n>39:12</n> Withhold not thou, O Lord, thy tender mercies from me: * thy mercy and thy truth have always upheld me.
<n>39:13</n> For evils without number have surrounded me; * my iniquities have overtaken me, and I was not able to see.
<n>39:13</n> They are multiplied above the hairs of my head: * and my heart hath forsaken me.
<n>39:14</n> Be pleased, O Lord to deliver me: * look down, O Lord, to help me.
03.e5283a3f17:
<n>39:15</n> Confundántur et revereántur simul, qui quærunt ánimam meam, * ut áuferant eam.
<n>39:15</n> Convertántur retrórsum, et revereántur, * qui volunt mihi mala.
<n>39:16</n> Ferant conféstim confusiónem suam, * qui dicunt mihi: Euge, euge.
<n>39:17</n> Exsúltent et læténtur super te omnes quæréntes te: * et dicant semper: Magnificétur Dóminus: qui díligunt salutáre tuum.
<n>39:18</n> Ego autem mendícus sum, et pauper: * Dóminus sollícitus est mei.
<n>39:18</n> Adjútor meus, et protéctor meus tu es: * Deus meus, ne tardáveris.
03.722ba70b05:
<n>39:15</n> Let them be confounded and ashamed together, that seek after my soul * to take it away.
<n>39:15</n> Let them be turned backward and be ashamed * that desire evils to me.
<n>39:16</n> Let them immediately bear their confusion, * that say to me: ’T is well, ’t is well.
<n>39:17</n> Let all that seek thee rejoice and be glad in thee: * and let such as love thy salvation say always: The Lord be magnified.
<n>39:18</n> But I am a beggar and poor: * the Lord is careful for me.
<n>39:18</n> Thou art my helper and my protector: * O my God, be not slack.
03.d6502e46bb:
<n>33:2</n> Benedícam Dóminum in omni témpore: * semper laus ejus in ore meo.
<n>33:3</n> In Dómino laudábitur ánima mea: * áudiant mansuéti, et læténtur.
<n>33:4</n> Magnificáte Dóminum mecum: * et exaltémus nomen ejus in idípsum.
<n>33:5</n> Exquisívi Dóminum, et exaudívit me: * et ex ómnibus tribulatiónibus meis erípuit me.
<n>33:6</n> Accédite ad eum, et illuminámini: * et fácies vestræ non confundéntur.
<n>33:7</n> Iste pauper clamávit, et Dóminus exaudívit eum: * et de ómnibus tribulatiónibus ejus salvávit eum.
<n>33:8</n> Immíttet Ángelus Dómini in circúitu timéntium eum: * et erípiet eos.
<n>33:9</n> Gustáte, et vidéte quóniam suávis est Dóminus: * beátus vir, qui sperat in eo.
<n>33:10</n> Timéte Dóminum, omnes sancti ejus: * quóniam non est inópia timéntibus eum.
<n>33:11</n> Dívites eguérunt et esuriérunt: * inquiréntes autem Dóminum non minuéntur omni bono.
03.632f4870ea:
<n>33:2</n> I will bless the Lord at all times, * his praise shall be always in my mouth.
<n>33:3</n> In the Lord shall my soul be praised: * let the meek hear and rejoice.
<n>33:4</n> O magnify the Lord with me; * and let us extol his name together.
<n>33:5</n> I sought the Lord, and he heard me; * and he delivered me from all my troubles.
<n>33:6</n> Come ye to him and be enlightened: * and your faces shall not be confounded.
<n>33:7</n> This poor man cried, and the Lord heard him: * and saved him out of all his troubles.
<n>33:8</n> The Angel of the Lord shall encamp round about them that fear him: * and shall deliver them.
<n>33:9</n> O taste, and see that the Lord is sweet: * blessed is the man that hopeth in him.
<n>33:10</n> Fear the Lord, all ye his saints: * for there is no want to them that fear him.
<n>33:11</n> The rich have wanted, and have suffered hunger: * but they that seek the Lord shall not be deprived of any good.
03.f88a95022b:
<n>33:12</n> Veníte, fílii, audíte me: * timórem Dómini docébo vos.
<n>33:13</n> Quis est homo qui vult vitam: * díligit dies vidére bonos?
<n>33:14</n> Próhibe linguam tuam a malo: * et lábia tua ne loquántur dolum.
<n>33:15</n> Divérte a malo, et fac bonum: * inquíre pacem, et perséquere eam.
<n>33:16</n> Óculi Dómini super justos: * et aures ejus in preces eórum.
<n>33:17</n> Vultus autem Dómini super faciéntes mala: * ut perdat de terra memóriam eórum.
<n>33:18</n> Clamavérunt justi, et Dóminus exaudívit eos: * et ex ómnibus tribulatiónibus eórum liberávit eos.
<n>33:19</n> Juxta est Dóminus iis, qui tribuláto sunt corde: * et húmiles spíritu salvábit.
<n>33:20</n> Multæ tribulatiónes justórum: * et de ómnibus his liberábit eos Dóminus.
<n>33:21</n> Custódit Dóminus ómnia ossa eórum: * unum ex his non conterétur.
<n>33:22</n> Mors peccatórum péssima: * et qui odérunt justum, delínquent.
<n>33:23</n> Rédimet Dóminus ánimas servórum suórum: * et non delínquent omnes qui sperant in eo.
03.1346f14966:
<n>33:12</n> Come, children, hearken to me: * I will teach you the fear of the Lord.
<n>33:13</n> Who is the man that desireth life: * who loveth to see good days?
<n>33:14</n> Keep thy tongue from evil, * and thy lips from speaking guile.
<n>33:15</n> Turn away from evil and do good: * seek after peace and pursue it.
<n>33:16</n> The eyes of the Lord are upon the just: * and his ears unto their prayers.
<n>33:17</n> But the countenance of the Lord is against them that do evil things: * to cut off the remembrance of them from the earth.
<n>33:18</n> The just cried, and the Lord heard them: * and delivered them out of all their troubles.
<n>33:19</n> The Lord is nigh unto them that are of a contrite heart: * and he will save the humble of spirit.
<n>33:20</n> Many are the afflictions of the just; * but out of them all will the Lord deliver them.
<n>33:21</n> The Lord keepeth all their bones, * not one of them shall be broken.
<n>33:22</n> The death of the wicked is very evil: * and they that hate the just shall be guilty.
<n>33:23</n> The Lord will redeem the souls of his servants: * and none of them that trust in him shall offend.
03.4050bf794c:
<n>35:2</n> Dixit injústus ut delínquat in semetípso: * non est timor Dei ante óculos ejus.
<n>35:3</n> Quóniam dolóse egit in conspéctu ejus: * ut inveniátur iníquitas ejus ad ódium.
<n>35:4</n> Verba oris ejus iníquitas, et dolus: * nóluit intellégere ut bene ágeret.
<n>35:5</n> Iniquitátem meditátus est in cubíli suo: * ástitit omni viæ non bonæ, malítiam autem non odívit.
<n>35:6</n> Dómine, in cælo misericórdia tua: * et véritas tua usque ad nubes.
<n>35:7</n> Justítia tua sicut montes Dei: * judícia tua abýssus multa.
<n>35:7</n> Hómines, et juménta salvábis, Dómine: * quemádmodum multiplicásti misericórdiam tuam, Deus.
<n>35:8</n> Fílii autem hóminum, * in tégmine alárum tuárum sperábunt.
<n>35:9</n> Inebriabúntur ab ubertáte domus tuæ: * et torrénte voluptátis tuæ potábis eos.
<n>35:10</n> Quóniam apud te est fons vitæ: * et in lúmine tuo vidébimus lumen.
<n>35:11</n> Præténde misericórdiam tuam sciéntibus te, * et justítiam tuam his, qui recto sunt corde.
<n>35:12</n> Non véniat mihi pes supérbiæ: * et manus peccatóris non móveat me.
<n>35:13</n> Ibi cecidérunt qui operántur iniquitátem: * expúlsi sunt, nec potuérunt stare.
03.41cba4f116:
<n>35:2</n> The unjust hath said within himself, that he would sin: * there is no fear of God before his eyes.
<n>35:3</n> For in his sight he hath done deceitfully, * that his iniquity may be found unto hatred.
<n>35:4</n> The words of his mouth are iniquity and guile: * he would not understand that he might do well.
<n>35:5</n> He hath devised iniquity on his bed, * he hath set himself on every way that is not good: but evil he hath not hated.
<n>35:6</n> O Lord, thy mercy is in heaven, * and thy truth reacheth even to the clouds.
<n>35:7</n> Thy justice is as the mountains of God, * thy judgments are a great deep.
<n>35:7</n> Men and beasts thou wilt preserve, O Lord: * O how hast thou multiplied thy mercy, O God!
<n>35:8</n> But the children of men * shall put their trust under the covert of thy wings.
<n>35:9</n> They shall be inebriated with the plenty of thy house; * and thou shalt make them drink of the torrent of thy pleasure.
<n>35:10</n> For with thee is the fountain of life; * and in thy light we shall see light.
<n>35:11</n> Extend thy mercy to them that know thee, * and thy justice to them that are right in heart.
<n>35:12</n> Let not the foot of pride come to me, * and let not the hand of the sinner move me.
<n>35:13</n> There the workers of iniquity are fallen, * they are cast out, and could not stand.
03.9d004a71db:
<n>31:10</n> Audíte verbum Dómini, gentes, * et annuntiáte in ínsulis, quæ procul sunt,
<n>31:11</n> Et dícite: Qui dispérsit Israël, congregábit eum: * et custódiet eum sicut pastor gregem suum.
<n>31:12</n> Redémit enim Dóminus Jacob, * et liberávit eum de manu potentióris.
<n>31:13</n> Et vénient, et laudábunt in monte Sion: * et cónfluent ad bona Dómini,
<n>31:14</n> Super fruménto, et vino, et óleo, * et fœtu pécorum et armentórum:
<n>31:15</n> Erítque ánima eórum quasi hortus irríguus, * et ultra non esúrient.
<n>31:16</n> Tunc lætábitur virgo in choro, * júvenes et senes simul:
<n>31:17</n> Et convértam luctum eórum in gáudium, * et consolábor eos, et lætificábo a dolóre suo.
<n>31:18</n> Et inebriábo ánimam sacerdótum pinguédine: * et pópulus meus bonis meis adimplébitur.
03.9e95089a43:
<n>31:10</n> Hear the word of the Lord, O ye nations, * and declare it in the islands that are afar off,
<n>31:11</n> And say: He that scattered Israel will gather him: * and he will keep him as the shepherd doth his flock.
<n>31:12</n> For the Lord hath redeemed Jacob, * and delivered him out of the hand of one that was mightier than he.
<n>31:13</n> And they shall come, and shall give praise in mount Sion: * and they shall flow together to the good things of the Lord,
<n>31:14</n> For the corn, and wine, and oil, * and the increase of cattle and herds,
<n>31:15</n> And their soul shall be as a watered garden, * and they shall be hungry no more.
<n>31:16</n> Then shall the virgin rejoice in the dance, * the young men and old men together:
<n>31:17</n> And I will turn their mourning into joy, * and will comfort them, and make them joyful after their sorrow.
<n>31:18</n> And I will fill the soul of the priests with fatness: * and my people shall be filled with my good things.
03.8657f9319b:
<n>36:1</n> Miserére nostri, Deus ómnium, et réspice nos, * et osténde nobis lucem miseratiónum tuárum:
<n>36:2</n> Et immítte timórem tuum super gentes, * quæ non exquisiérunt te,
<n>36:3</n> Ut cognóscant quia non est Deus nisi tu, * et enárrent magnália tua.
<n>36:4</n> Álleva manum tuam super gentes aliénas, * ut vídeant poténtiam tuam.
<n>36:5</n> Sicut enim in conspéctu eórum sanctificátus es in nobis, * sic in conspéctu nostro magnificáberis in eis,
<n>36:6</n> Ut cognóscant te, sicut et nos cognóvimus, * quóniam non est Deus præter te, Dómine.
<n>36:7</n> Ínnova signa, et immúta mirabília. * Glorífica manum, et brácchium dextrum.
<n>36:8</n> Éxcita furórem, et effúnde iram. * Tolle adversárium, et afflíge inimícum.
<n>36:9</n> Festína tempus, et meménto finis, * ut enárrent mirabília tua.
<n>36:10</n> In ira flammæ devorétur qui salvátur: * et qui péssimant plebem tuam, invéniant perditiónem.
<n>36:11</n> Cóntere caput príncipum inimicórum, * dicéntium: Non est álius præter nos.
<n>36:12</n> Cóngrega omnes tribus Jacob: ut cognóscant quia non est Deus nisi tu, * et enárrent magnália tua:
<n>36:13</n> Et hereditábis eos, * sicut ab inítio.
<n>36:14</n> Miserére plebi tuæ, super quam invocátum est nomen tuum: * et Israël, quem coæquásti primogénito tuo.
<n>36:15</n> Miserére civitáti sanctificatiónis tuæ Jerúsalem, * civitáti requiéi tuæ.
<n>36:16</n> Reple Sion inenarrabílibus verbis tuis, * et glória tua pópulum tuum.
03.d2933cb1b8:
<n>36:1</n> Have mercy upon us, O God of all, and behold us, * and shew us the light of thy mercies:
<n>36:2</n> And send thy fear upon the nations, * that have not sought after thee:
<n>36:3</n> That they may know that there is no God beside thee, * and that they may shew forth thy wonders.
<n>36:4</n> Lift up thy hand over the strange nations, * that they may see thy power.
<n>36:5</n> For as thou hast been sanctified in us in their sight, * so thou shalt be magnified among them in our presence,
<n>36:6</n> That they may know thee, as we also have known thee, * that there is no God beside thee, O Lord.
<n>36:7</n> Renew thy signs, and work new miracles. * Glorify thy hand, and thy right arm.
<n>36:8</n> Raise up indignation, and pour out wrath. * Take away the adversary, and crush the enemy.
<n>36:9</n> Hasten the time, and remember the end, * that they may declare thy wonderful works.
<n>36:10</n> Let him that escapeth be consumed by the rage of the fire: * and let them perish that oppress thy people.
<n>36:11</n> Crush the head of the princes of the enemies * that say: There is no other beside us.
<n>36:12</n> Gather together all the tribes of Jacob: that they may know that there is no God besides thee, * and may declare thy great works.
<n>36:13</n> And thou shalt inherit them * as from the beginning.
<n>36:14</n> Have mercy on thy people, upon whom thy name is invoked: * and upon Israel, whom thou hast raised up to be thy firstborn.
<n>36:15</n> Have mercy on Jerusalem, the city which thou hast sanctified, * the city of thy rest.
<n>36:16</n> Fill Sion with thy unspeakable words, * and thy people with thy glory.
03.7b4891780b:
<n>30:2</n> In te, Dómine, sperávi, non confúndar in ætérnum: * in justítia tua líbera me.
<n>30:3</n> Inclína ad me aurem tuam, * accélera ut éruas me.
<n>30:3</n> Esto mihi in Deum protectórem, et in domum refúgii: * ut salvum me fácias.
<n>30:4</n> Quóniam fortitúdo mea, et refúgium meum es tu: * et propter nomen tuum dedúces me, et enútries me.
<n>30:5</n> Edúces me de láqueo hoc, quem abscondérunt mihi: * quóniam tu es protéctor meus.
<n>30:6</n> In manus tuas comméndo spíritum meum: * redemísti me, Dómine, Deus veritátis.
<n>30:7</n> Odísti observántes vanitátes, * supervácue.
<n>30:7</n> Ego autem in Dómino sperávi: * exsultábo, et lætábor in misericórdia tua.
<n>30:8</n> Quóniam respexísti humilitátem meam, * salvásti de necessitátibus ánimam meam.
<n>30:9</n> Nec conclusísti me in mánibus inimíci: * statuísti in loco spatióso pedes meos.
03.b19ea80ea5:
<n>30:2</n> In thee, O Lord, have I hoped, let me never be confounded: * deliver me in thy justice.
<n>30:3</n> Bow down thy ear to me: * make haste to deliver me.
<n>30:3</n> Be thou unto me a God, a protector, and a house of refuge, * to save me.
<n>30:4</n> For thou art my strength and my refuge; * and for thy name’s sake thou wilt lead me, and nourish me.
<n>30:5</n> Thou wilt bring me out of this snare, which they have hidden for me: * for thou art my protector.
<n>30:6</n> Into thy hands I commend my spirit: * thou hast redeemed me, O Lord, the God of truth.
<n>30:7</n> Thou hast hated them that regard vanities, * to no purpose.
<n>30:7</n> But I have hoped in the Lord: * I will be glad and rejoice in thy mercy.
<n>30:8</n> For thou hast regarded my humility, * thou hast saved my soul out of distresses.
<n>30:9</n> And thou hast not shut me up in the hands of the enemy: * thou hast set my feet in a spacious place.
03.fbb7dfab4d:
<n>30:10</n> Miserére mei, Dómine, quóniam tríbulor: * conturbátus est in ira óculus meus, ánima mea, et venter meus:
<n>30:11</n> Quóniam defécit in dolóre vita mea: * et anni mei in gemítibus.
<n>30:11</n> Infirmáta est in paupertáte virtus mea: * et ossa mea conturbáta sunt.
<n>30:12</n> Super omnes inimícos meos factus sum oppróbrium et vicínis meis valde: * et timor notis meis.
<n>30:12</n> Qui vidébant me, foras fugérunt a me: * oblivióni datus sum, tamquam mórtuus a corde.
<n>30:13</n> Factus sum tamquam vas pérditum: * quóniam audívi vituperatiónem multórum commorántium in circúitu.
<n>30:14</n> In eo dum convenírent simul advérsum me, * accípere ánimam meam consiliáti sunt.
<n>30:15</n> Ego autem in te sperávi, Dómine: * dixi: Deus meus es tu: in mánibus tuis sortes meæ.
<n>30:16</n> Éripe me de manu inimicórum meórum, * et a persequéntibus me.
<n>30:17</n> Illústra fáciem tuam super servum tuum, salvum me fac in misericórdia tua: * Dómine, non confúndar, quóniam invocávi te.
<n>30:18</n> Erubéscant ímpii, et deducántur in inférnum: * muta fiant lábia dolósa.
<n>30:19</n> Quæ loquúntur advérsus justum iniquitátem: * in supérbia, et in abusióne.
03.04135fd0ce:
<n>30:10</n> Have mercy on me, O Lord, for I am afflicted: * my eye is troubled with wrath, my soul, and my belly:
<n>30:11</n> For my life is wasted with grief: * and my years in sighs.
<n>30:11</n> My strength is weakened through poverty * and my bones are disturbed.
<n>30:12</n> I am become a reproach among all my enemies, and very much to my neighbours; * and a fear to my acquaintance.
<n>30:12</n> They that saw me without fled from me. * I am forgotten as one dead from the heart.
<n>30:13</n> I am become as a vessel that is destroyed. * For I have heard the blame of many that dwell round about.
<n>30:14</n> While they assembled together against me, * they consulted to take away my life.
<n>30:15</n> But I have put my trust in thee, O Lord: * I said: Thou art my God. My lots are in thy hands.
<n>30:16</n> Deliver me out of the hands of my enemies; * and from them that persecute me.
<n>30:17</n> Make thy face to shine upon thy servant; save me in thy mercy. * Let me not be confounded, O Lord, for I have called upon thee.
<n>30:18</n> Let the wicked be ashamed, and be brought down to hell. * Let deceitful lips be made dumb.
<n>30:19</n> Which speak iniquity against the just, * with pride and abuse.
03.a03cffbd5b:
<n>30:20</n> Quam magna multitúdo dulcédinis tuæ, Dómine, * quam abscondísti timéntibus te.
<n>30:20</n> Perfecísti eis, qui sperant in te, * in conspéctu filiórum hóminum.
<n>30:21</n> Abscóndes eos in abscóndito faciéi tuæ * a conturbatióne hóminum.
<n>30:21</n> Próteges eos in tabernáculo tuo * a contradictióne linguárum.
<n>30:22</n> Benedíctus Dóminus: * quóniam mirificávit misericórdiam suam mihi in civitáte muníta.
<n>30:23</n> Ego autem dixi in excéssu mentis meæ: * Projéctus sum a fácie oculórum tuórum.
<n>30:23</n> Ídeo exaudísti vocem oratiónis meæ, * dum clamárem ad te.
<n>30:24</n> Dilígite Dóminum omnes sancti ejus: * quóniam veritátem requíret Dóminus, et retríbuet abundánter faciéntibus supérbiam.
<n>30:25</n> Viríliter ágite, et confortétur cor vestrum, * omnes, qui sperátis in Dómino.
03.f6c00354d3:
<n>30:20</n> How great is the multitude of thy sweetness, O Lord, * which thou hast hidden for them that fear thee!
<n>30:20</n> Which thou hast wrought for them that hope in thee, * in the sight of the sons of men.
<n>30:21</n> Thou shalt hide them in the secret of thy face, * from the disturbance of men.
<n>30:21</n> Thou shalt protect them in thy tabernacle * from the contradiction of tongues.
<n>30:22</n> Blessed be the Lord, * for he hath shewn his wonderful mercy to me in a fortified city.
<n>30:23</n> But I said in the excess of my mind: * I am cast away from before thy eyes.
<n>30:23</n> Therefore thou hast heard the voice of my prayer, * when I cried to thee.
<n>30:24</n> O love the Lord, all ye his saints: * for the Lord will require truth, and will repay them abundantly that act proudly.
<n>30:25</n> Do ye manfully, and let your heart be strengthened, * all ye that hope in the Lord.
03.8afc5c2f4a:
<n>31:1</n> Beáti quorum remíssæ sunt iniquitátes: * et quorum tecta sunt peccáta.
<n>31:2</n> Beátus vir, cui non imputávit Dóminus peccátum, * nec est in spíritu ejus dolus.
<n>31:3</n> Quóniam tácui, inveteravérunt ossa mea, * dum clamárem tota die.
<n>31:4</n> Quóniam die ac nocte graváta est super me manus tua: * convérsus sum in ærúmna mea, dum confígitur spina.
<n>31:5</n> Delíctum meum cógnitum tibi feci: * et injustítiam meam non abscóndi.
<n>31:5</n> Dixi: Confitébor advérsum me injustítiam meam Dómino: * et tu remisísti impietátem peccáti mei.
<n>31:6</n> Pro hac orábit ad te omnis sanctus, * in témpore opportúno.
<n>31:6</n> Verúmtamen in dilúvio aquárum multárum, * ad eum non approximábunt.
<n>31:7</n> Tu es refúgium meum a tribulatióne, quæ circúmdedit me: * exsultátio mea, érue me a circumdántibus me.
<n>31:8</n> Intelléctum tibi dabo, et ínstruam te in via hac, qua gradiéris: * firmábo super te óculos meos.
<n>31:9</n> Nolíte fíeri sicut equus et mulus, * quibus non est intelléctus.
<n>31:9</n> In camo et freno maxíllas eórum constrínge, * qui non appróximant ad te.
<n>31:10</n> Multa flagélla peccatóris, * sperántem autem in Dómino misericórdia circúmdabit.
<n>31:11</n> Lætámini in Dómino et exsultáte, justi, * et gloriámini, omnes recti corde.
03.8271602ab9:
<n>31:1</n> Blessed are those whose iniquities are forgiven * and whose sins are covered.
<n>31:2</n> Blessed is the man to whom the Lord hath not imputed sin, * and in whose spirit there is no guile.
<n>31:3</n> Because I was silent my bones grew old; * whilst I cried out all the day long.
<n>31:4</n> For day and night thy hand was heavy upon me: * I am turned in my anguish, whilst the thorn is fastened.
<n>31:5</n> I have acknowledged my sin to thee, * and my injustice I have not concealed.
<n>31:5</n> I said I will confess against myself my injustice to the Lord: * and thou hast forgiven the wickedness of my sin.
<n>31:6</n> For this shall every one that is holy pray to thee * in a seasonable time.
<n>31:6</n> And yet in a flood of many waters, * they shall not come nigh unto him.
<n>31:7</n> Thou art my refuge from the trouble which hath encompassed me: * my joy, deliver me from them that surround me.
<n>31:8</n> I will give thee understanding, and I will instruct thee in this way, in which thou shalt go: * I will fix my eyes upon thee.
<n>31:9</n> Do not become like the horse and the mule, * who have no understanding.
<n>31:9</n> With bit and bridle bind fast their jaws, * who come not near unto thee.
<n>31:10</n> Many are the scourges of the sinner, * but mercy shall encompass him that hopeth in the Lord.
<n>31:11</n> Be glad in the Lord, and rejoice, ye just, * and glory, all ye right of heart.
03.bbcdaae8f9:
<n>32:1</n> Exsultáte, justi, in Dómino: * rectos decet collaudátio.
<n>32:2</n> Confitémini Dómino in cíthara: * in psaltério decem chordárum psállite illi.
<n>32:3</n> Cantáte ei cánticum novum: * bene psállite ei in vociferatióne.
<n>32:4</n> Quia rectum est verbum Dómini, * et ómnia ópera ejus in fide.
<n>32:5</n> Díligit misericórdiam et judícium: * misericórdia Dómini plena est terra.
<n>32:6</n> Verbo Dómini cæli firmáti sunt: * et spíritu oris ejus omnis virtus eórum.
<n>32:7</n> Cóngregans sicut in utre aquas maris: * ponens in thesáuris abýssos.
<n>32:8</n> Tímeat Dóminum omnis terra: * ab eo autem commoveántur omnes inhabitántes orbem.
<n>32:9</n> Quóniam ipse dixit, et facta sunt: * ipse mandávit, et creáta sunt.
<n>32:10</n> Dóminus díssipat consília géntium: * réprobat autem cogitatiónes populórum, et réprobat consília príncipum.
<n>32:11</n> Consílium autem Dómini in ætérnum manet: * cogitatiónes cordis ejus in generatióne et generatiónem.
03.a973fd5e8b:
<n>32:1</n> Rejoice in the Lord, O ye just: * praise becometh the upright.
<n>32:2</n> Give praise to the Lord on the harp; * sing to him with the psaltery, the instrument of ten strings.
<n>32:3</n> Sing to him a new canticle, * sing well unto him with a loud noise.
<n>32:4</n> For the word of the Lord is right, * and all his works are done with faithfulness.
<n>32:5</n> He loveth mercy and judgment; * the earth is full of the mercy of the Lord.
<n>32:6</n> By the word of the Lord the heavens were established; * and all the power of them by the spirit of his mouth:
<n>32:7</n> Gathering together the waters of the sea, as in a vessel; * laying up the depths in storehouses.
<n>32:8</n> Let all the earth fear the Lord, * and let all the inhabitants of the world be in awe of him.
<n>32:9</n> For he spoke and they were made: * he commanded and they were created.
<n>32:10</n> The Lord bringeth to nought the counsels of nations; * and he rejecteth the devices of people, and casteth away the counsels of princes.
<n>32:11</n> But the counsel of the Lord standeth for ever: * the thoughts of his heart to all generations.
03.295b65e54d:
<n>32:12</n> Beáta gens, cujus est Dóminus, Deus ejus: * pópulus, quem elégit in hereditátem sibi.
<n>32:13</n> De cælo respéxit Dóminus: * vidit omnes fílios hóminum.
<n>32:14</n> De præparáto habitáculo suo * respéxit super omnes, qui hábitant terram.
<n>32:15</n> Qui finxit sigillátim corda eórum: * qui intéllegit ómnia ópera eórum.
<n>32:16</n> Non salvátur rex per multam virtútem: * et gigas non salvábitur in multitúdine virtútis suæ.
<n>32:17</n> Fallax equus ad salútem: * in abundántia autem virtútis suæ non salvábitur.
<n>32:18</n> Ecce, óculi Dómini super metuéntes eum: * et in eis, qui sperant super misericórdia ejus:
<n>32:19</n> Ut éruat a morte ánimas eórum: * et alat eos in fame.
<n>32:20</n> Ánima nostra sústinet Dóminum: * quóniam adjútor et protéctor noster est.
<n>32:21</n> Quia in eo lætábitur cor nostrum: * et in nómine sancto ejus sperávimus.
<n>32:22</n> Fiat misericórdia tua, Dómine, super nos: * quemádmodum sperávimus in te.
03.444832b554:
<n>32:12</n> Blessed is the nation whose God is the Lord: * the people whom he hath chosen for his inheritance.
<n>32:13</n> The Lord hath looked from heaven: * he hath beheld all the sons of men.
<n>32:14</n> From his habitation which he hath prepared, * he hath looked upon all that dwell on the earth.
<n>32:15</n> He who hath made the hearts of every one of them: * who understandeth all their works.
<n>32:16</n> The king is not saved by a great army: * nor shall the giant be saved by his own great strength.
<n>32:17</n> Vain is the horse for safety: * neither shall he be saved by the abundance of his strength.
<n>32:18</n> Behold the eyes of the Lord are on them that fear him: * and on them that hope in his mercy.
<n>32:19</n> To deliver their souls from death; * and feed them in famine.
<n>32:20</n> Our soul waiteth for the Lord: * for he is our helper and protector.
<n>32:21</n> For in him our heart shall rejoice: * and in his holy name we have trusted.
<n>32:22</n> Let thy mercy, O Lord, be upon us, * as we have hoped in thee.
03.413e92455c:
<n>32:1</n> Audíte, cæli, quæ loquor: * áudiat terra verba oris mei.
<n>32:2</n> Concréscat ut plúvia doctrína mea, * fluat ut ros elóquium meum.
<n>32:3</n> Quasi imber super herbam, et quasi stillæ super grámina. * Quia nomen Dómini invocábo.
<n>32:4</n> Date magnificéntiam Deo nostro. * Dei perfécta sunt ópera, et omnes viæ ejus judícia:
<n>32:5</n> Deus fidélis, et absque ulla iniquitáte, justus et rectus. * Peccavérunt ei, et non fílii ejus in sórdibus:
<n>32:6</n> Generátio prava atque pervérsa. * Hǽccine reddis Dómino, pópule stulte et insípiens?
<n>32:7</n> Numquid non ipse est pater tuus, * qui possédit te, et fecit, et creávit te?
<n>32:8</n> Meménto diérum antiquórum, * cógita generatiónes síngulas:
<n>32:9</n> Intérroga patrem tuum, et annuntiábit tibi: * majóres tuos, et dicent tibi.
<n>32:10</n> Quando dividébat Altíssimus gentes: * quando separábat fílios Adam.
<n>32:11</n> Constítuit términos populórum * juxta númerum filiórum Israël.
<n>32:12</n> Pars autem Dómini, pópulus ejus: * Jacob funículus hereditátis ejus.
<n>32:13</n> Invénit eum in terra desérta, * in loco horróris et vastæ solitúdinis:
<n>32:14</n> Circumdúxit eum, et dócuit: * et custodívit quasi pupíllam óculi sui.
<n>32:15</n> Sicut áquila próvocans ad volándum pullos suos, * et super eos vólitans,
<n>32:16</n> Expándit alas suas, et assúmpsit eum, * atque portávit in húmeris suis.
<n>32:17</n> Dóminus solus dux ejus fuit: * et non erat cum eo deus aliénus.
<n>32:18</n> Constítuit eum super excélsam terram: * ut coméderet fructus agrórum,
<n>32:19</n> Ut súgeret mel de petra, * oleúmque de saxo duríssimo.
<n>32:20</n> Butýrum de arménto, et lac de óvibus * cum ádipe agnórum, et aríetum filiórum Basan:
<n>32:21</n> Et hircos cum medúlla trítici, * et sánguinem uvæ bíberet meracíssimum.
<n>32:22</n> Incrassátus est diléctus, et recalcitrávit: * incrassátus, impinguátus, dilatátus,
<n>32:23</n> Derelíquit Deum, factórem suum, * et recéssit a Deo, salutári suo.
<n>32:24</n> Provocavérunt eum in diis aliénis, * et in abominatiónibus ad iracúndiam concitavérunt.
<n>32:25</n> Immolavérunt dæmóniis, et non Deo, * diis, quos ignorábant:
<n>32:26</n> Novi recentésque venérunt, * quos non coluérunt patres eórum.
<n>32:27</n> Deum qui te génuit dereliquísti, * et oblítus es Dómini, creatóris tui.
<n>32:28</n> Vidit Dóminus, et ad iracúndiam concitátus est: * quia provocavérunt eum fílii sui et fíliæ.
<n>32:29</n> Et ait: Abscóndam fáciem meam ab eis, * et considerábo novíssima eórum:
<n>32:30</n> Generátio enim pervérsa est, * et infidéles fílii.
<n>32:31</n> Ipsi me provocavérunt in eo, qui non erat Deus, * et irritavérunt in vanitátibus suis:
<n>32:32</n> Et ego provocábo eos in eo, qui non est pópulus, * et in gente stulta irritábo illos.
<n>32:33</n> Ignis succénsus est in furóre meo, * et ardébit usque ad inférni novíssima:
<n>32:34</n> Devorabítque terram cum gérmine suo, * et móntium fundaménta combúret.
<n>32:35</n> Congregábo super eos mala, * et sagíttas meas complébo in eis.
<n>32:36</n> Consuméntur fame, * et devorábunt eos aves morsu amaríssimo:
<n>32:37</n> Dentes bestiárum immíttam in eos, * cum furóre trahéntium super terram, atque serpéntium.
<n>32:38</n> Foris vastábit eos gládius, et intus pavor, * júvenem simul ac vírginem, lactántem cum hómine sene.
<n>32:39</n> Dixi: Ubinam sunt? * cessáre fáciam ex homínibus memóriam eórum.
<n>32:40</n> Sed propter iram inimicórum dístuli: * ne forte superbírent hostes eórum,
<n>32:41</n> Et dícerent: Manus nostra excélsa, et non Dóminus, * fecit hæc ómnia.
<n>32:42</n> Gens absque consílio est, et sine prudéntia. * Utinam sáperent, et intellégerent, ac novíssima providérent.
<n>32:43</n> Quómodo persequátur unus mille, * et duo fugent decem míllia?
<n>32:44</n> Nonne ídeo, quia Deus suus véndidit eos, * et Dóminus conclúsit illos?
<n>32:45</n> Non enim est Deus noster ut dii eórum: * et inimíci nostri sunt júdices.
<n>32:46</n> De vínea Sodomórum vínea eórum, * et de suburbánis Gomórrhæ:
<n>32:47</n> Uva eórum uva fellis, * et botri amaríssimi.
<n>32:48</n> Fel dracónum vinum eórum, * et venénum áspidum insanábile.
<n>32:49</n> Nonne hæc cóndita sunt apud me, * et signáta in thesáuris meis?
<n>32:50</n> Mea est últio, et ego retríbuam in témpore, * ut labátur pes eórum:
<n>32:51</n> Juxta est dies perditiónis, * et adésse festínant témpora.
<n>32:52</n> Judicábit Dóminus pópulum suum, * et in servis suis miserébitur:
<n>32:53</n> Vidébit quod infirmáta sit manus, * et clausi quoque defecérunt, residuíque consúmpti sunt.
<n>32:54</n> Et dicet: Ubi sunt dii eórum, * in quibus habébant fidúciam?
<n>32:55</n> De quorum víctimis comedébant ádipes, * et bibébant vinum libáminum:
<n>32:56</n> Surgant, et opituléntur vobis, * et in necessitáte vos prótegant.
<n>32:57</n> Vidéte quod ego sim solus, * et non sit álius Deus præter me:
<n>32:58</n> Ego occídam, et ego vívere fáciam: percútiam, et ego sanábo, * et non est qui de manu mea possit erúere.
<n>32:59</n> Levábo ad cælum manum meam, et dicam: * Vivo ego in ætérnum.
<n>32:60</n> Si acúero ut fulgur gládium meum, * et arripúerit judícium manus mea:
<n>32:61</n> Reddam ultiónem hóstibus meis, * et his qui odérunt me retríbuam.
<n>32:62</n> Inebriábo sagíttas meas sánguine, * et gládius meus devorábit carnes,
<n>32:63</n> De cruóre occisórum, * et de captivitáte, nudáti inimicórum cápitis.
<n>32:64</n> Laudáte, gentes, pópulum ejus, * quia sánguinem servórum suórum ulciscétur:
<n>32:65</n> Et vindíctam retríbuet in hostes eórum, * et propítius erit terræ pópuli sui.
03.a645e02187:
<n>32:1</n> Hear, O ye heavens, the things I speak, * let the earth give ear to the words of my mouth.
<n>32:2</n> Let my doctrine gather as the rain, * let my speech distill as the dew,
<n>32:3</n> As a shower upon the herb, and as drops upon the grass. * Because I will invoke the name of the Lord:
<n>32:4</n> Give ye magnificence to our God. * The works of God are perfect, and all his ways are judgments:
<n>32:5</n> God is faithful and without any iniquity, he is just and right. * They have sinned against him, and are none of his children in their filth:
<n>32:6</n> They are a wicked and perverse generation. * Is this the return thou makest to the Lord, O foolish and senseless people?
<n>32:7</n> Is not he thy father, * that hath possessed thee, and made thee, and created thee?
<n>32:8</n> Remember the days of old, * think upon every generation:
<n>32:9</n> Ask thy father, and he will declare to thee: * thy elders and they will tell thee.
<n>32:10</n> When the Most High divided the nations: * when he separated the sons of Adam,
<n>32:11</n> He appointed the bounds of people * according to the number of the children of Israel.
<n>32:12</n> But the Lord’s portion is his people: * Jacob the lot of his inheritance.
<n>32:13</n> He found him in a desert land, * in a place of horror, and of vast wilderness:
<n>32:14</n> He led him about, and taught him: * and he kept him as the apple of his eye.
<n>32:15</n> As the eagle enticing her young to fly, * and hovering over them,
<n>32:16</n> He spread his wings, and hath taken him * and carried him on his shoulders.
<n>32:17</n> The Lord alone was his leader: * and there was no strange god with him.
<n>32:18</n> He set him upon high land: * that he might eat the fruits of the fields,
<n>32:19</n> That he might suck honey out of the rock, * and oil out of the hardest stone,
<n>32:20</n> Butter of the herd, and milk of the sheep * with the fat of lambs, and of the rams of the breed of Basan:
<n>32:21</n> And goats with the marrow of wheat, * and might drink the purest blood of the grape.
<n>32:22</n> The beloved grew fat, and kicked: * he grew fat, and thick and gross,
<n>32:23</n> He forsook God who made him, * and departed from God his saviour.
<n>32:24</n> They provoked him by strange gods, * and stirred him up to anger, with their abominations.
<n>32:25</n> They sacrificed to devils and not to God: * to gods whom they knew not:
<n>32:26</n> That were newly come up, * whom their fathers worshipped not.
<n>32:27</n> Thou hast forsaken the God that beget * and hast forgotten the Lord that created thee.
<n>32:28</n> The Lord saw, and was moved to wrath: * because his own sons and daughters provoked him.
<n>32:29</n> And he said: I will hide my face from them, * and will consider what their last end shall be:
<n>32:30</n> for it is a perverse generation, * and unfaithful children.
<n>32:31</n> They have provoked me with that which was no god, * and have angered me with their vanities:
<n>32:32</n> and I will provoke them with that which is no people, * and will vex them with a foolish nation.
<n>32:33</n> A fire is kindled in my wrath, * and shall burn even to the lowest hell:
<n>32:34</n> and shall devour the earth with her increase, * and shall burn the foundations of the mountains.
<n>32:35</n> I will heap evils upon them, * and will spend my arrows among them.
<n>32:36</n> They shall be consumed with famine, * and birds shall devour them with a most bitter bite:
<n>32:37</n> I will send the teeth of beasts upon them, * with the fury of creatures that trail upon the ground, and of serpents.
<n>32:38</n> Without, the sword shall lay them waste, and terror within, * both the young man and the virgin, the sucking child with the man in years.
<n>32:39</n> I said: Where are they? * I will make the memory of them to cease from among men.
<n>32:40</n> But for the wrath of the enemies * I have deferred it: lest perhaps their enemies might be proud,
<n>32:41</n> and should say: Our mighty hand, and not the Lord, * hath done all these things.
<n>32:42</n> They are a nation without counsel, and without wisdom * O that they would be wise and would understand, and would provide for their last end.
<n>32:43</n> How should one pursue after a thousand, * and two chase ten thousand?
<n>32:44</n> Was it not, because their God had sold them, * and the Lord had shut them up?
<n>32:45</n> For our God is not as their gods: * our enemies themselves are judges.
<n>32:46</n> Their vines are of the vineyard of Sodom, * and of the suburbs of Gomorrha:
<n>32:47</n> their grapes are grapes of gall, * and their clusters most bitter.
<n>32:48</n> Their wine is the gall of dragons, * and the venom of asps, which is incurable.
<n>32:49</n> Are not these things stored up with me, * and sealed up in my treasures?
<n>32:50</n> Revenge is mine, and I will repay them in due time, * that their foot may slide:
<n>32:51</n> the day of destruction is at hand, * and the time makes haste to come.
<n>32:52</n> The Lord will judge his people, * and will have mercy on his servants:
<n>32:53</n> he shall see that their hand is weakened, * and that they who were shut up have also failed, and they that remained are consumed.
<n>32:54</n> And he shall say: Where are their gods, * in whom they trusted?
<n>32:55</n> Of whose victims they ate the fat, * and drank the wine of their drink offerings:
<n>32:56</n> let them arise and help you, * and protect you in your distress.
<n>32:57</n> See ye that I alone am, * and there is no other God besides me:
<n>32:58</n> I will kill and I will make to live: I will strike, and I will heal, * and there is none that can deliver out of my hand.
<n>32:59</n> I will lift up my hand to heaven, * and I will say: I live for ever.
<n>32:60</n> If I shall whet my sword as the lightning, * and my hand take hold on judgment:
<n>32:61</n> I will render vengeance to my enemies, * and repay them that hate me.
<n>32:62</n> I will make my arrows drunk with blood, * and my sword shall devour flesh,
<n>32:63</n> of the blood of the slain * and of the captivity, of the bare head of the enemies.
<n>32:64</n> Praise his people, ye nations, * for he will revenge the blood of his servants:
<n>32:65</n> and will render vengeance to their enemies, * and he will be merciful to the land of his people.
03.76c571b247:
<n>37:2</n> Dómine, ne in furóre tuo árguas me, * neque in ira tua corrípias me.
<n>37:3</n> Quóniam sagíttæ tuæ infíxæ sunt mihi: * et confirmásti super me manum tuam.
<n>37:4</n> Non est sánitas in carne mea a fácie iræ tuæ: * non est pax óssibus meis a fácie peccatórum meórum.
<n>37:5</n> Quóniam iniquitátes meæ supergréssæ sunt caput meum: * et sicut onus grave gravátæ sunt super me.
<n>37:6</n> Putruérunt et corrúptæ sunt cicatríces meæ, * a fácie insipiéntiæ meæ.
<n>37:7</n> Miser factus sum, et curvátus sum usque in finem: * tota die contristátus ingrediébar.
<n>37:8</n> Quóniam lumbi mei impléti sunt illusiónibus: * et non est sánitas in carne mea.
<n>37:9</n> Afflíctus sum, et humiliátus sum nimis: * rugiébam a gémitu cordis mei.
<n>37:10</n> Dómine, ante te omne desidérium meum: * et gémitus meus a te non est abscónditus.
